question: What attention-head pathways support few-shot chain-of-thought generation by Llama-2 7B on controlled multi-hop fictional-ontology questions?

key_findings.claim: The paper decomposes a fixed ten-token-step reasoning trace into decision, copying, and induction subtasks and finds broadly shared head sets rather than separate modules.
key_findings.evidence: Activation-patching scores identify attention heads for each subtask type; keeping heads ranked through the induction task preserves over 90% relative performance with roughly 400 of 1,024 heads, while task-only selections overlap substantially.

key_findings.claim: Ontology-relation information becomes nonlinearly decodable from paired residual streams and peaks around layers 10-15.
key_findings.evidence: Four-layer ReLU probes distinguish positive, negative, and unrelated fictional-entity pairs increasingly well through early/middle layers, while linear probes fail. Few-shot count has little effect on peak performance, suggesting this diagnostic is not itself evidence of prompt-induced token movement.

key_findings.claim: Several diagnostics change near the midpoint of Llama-2 7B, motivating a functional-rift hypothesis.
key_findings.evidence: Head-output vocabulary projections become more context-abiding after layer 16; ontology-pair probe accuracy peaks near that region; and all detected answer-writing heads lie in later layers. These co-located correlations do not establish a discrete causal phase transition.

key_findings.claim: The traced graphs contain multiple candidate answer routes from the question, prior generated steps, and occasionally few-shot examples.
key_findings.evidence: Starting from late heads whose direct-logit projection favors the answer, the authors recursively follow high-attention source positions and earlier heads. Induction subtasks 5 and 9 draw more often from generated context, whereas early copying/decision steps rely on question context; some early paths pull same-token occurrences from demonstrations in mismatched roles.

key_findings.claim: The evidence does not yet establish complete causal circuits or general CoT mechanisms.
key_findings.evidence: Head paths are constructed with attention weights and unembedding projections after an initial mean-ablation screen; probes and logit-lens tokens are correlational, no end-to-end path intervention validates individual algorithms, and MLP contributions are excluded. Only one model, one templated dataset, correct traces, and few-shot prompting are analyzed.

method.core_idea: Use controlled fictional facts and a fixed chain-of-thought template to localize and visualize attention components that move relation and answer information through a production LLM.
method.mechanism: Run Llama-2 7B on PrOntoQA few-shot prompts, split correct generations into ten decision/copy/induction positions, rank heads with noisy-versus-clean activation patching, and mean-ablate lower-ranked heads. Train layerwise probes on paired entity residuals, use direct-logit projections to label head outputs, compute contextual bigram-abidance, and recursively trace attention-source positions backward from late answer-writing heads.
assumptions: Fictional ontology tokens minimize pretrained factual-memory and MLP involvement while retaining representative reasoning mechanisms.
Mean activations from false-ontology examples are a neutral intervention baseline.
Direct unembedding of individual head outputs gives a meaningful token-level account despite residual-stream basis and downstream composition.
High attention to a source token along selected heads approximates causal information flow.
A fixed correct ten-subtask trace can stand in for freer and potentially erroneous chain-of-thought.

techniques.role: Maps fixed generation positions to decision, copy, and induction operations.
Scores which attention heads restore clean output distributions after perturbation.
Tests reduced head sets while avoiding destructive zero ablation.
Measures decodability of ontology relations from residual-stream pairs.
Labels answer-writing and context-abiding head outputs in vocabulary space.
Builds proposed source-to-answer graphs across question, generated, and demonstration contexts.

evaluations.setting: Llama-2 7B few-shot correct generations on PrOntoQA fictional ontology problems, divided into ten subtasks.
evaluations.metric: Relative token accuracy after head ablation and overlap/size of retained head sets.
evaluations.result: An induction-ranked subset of roughly 40% of heads retains above 90% performance across subtasks, with subtask 0 and induction step 5 most sensitive.
evaluations.baseline: Full model and task-specific head subsets.

evaluations.setting: Positive, negative, and unrelated fictional-entity pairs at every decoder layer with zero to four demonstrations.
evaluations.metric: Three-way linear and four-layer-ReLU probe accuracy.
evaluations.result: Only nonlinear probes strongly separate relations; accuracy rises from early layers, peaks around layers 10-15, and then falls, with little peak change across shot counts.

evaluations.setting: Per-subtask vocabulary projections and backward information-flow trees.
evaluations.metric: Context-abidance, answer probability in head output, source-context category, and attention paths.
evaluations.result: Answer-writing heads occur after layer 16; multiple proposed paths read answer tokens from sources whose distribution changes by subtask, with generated-context sources concentrated in induction steps.
evaluations.baseline: Comparisons across layers, subtasks, and question/generated/few-shot context segments.

limitations: One model family/size, a synthetic fictional ontology, a rigid few-shot trace, and filtered correct generations sharply limit generality.
Attention weights, nonlinear probes, and direct-logit projections reveal availability or association, not necessarily causal computation.
Recursive graphs are not validated through path-specific sufficiency and necessity interventions or independent causal scrubbing.
The head-selection importance score is unconventional and symmetric deviation from its mean can conflate very different patching behaviors.
MLPs are intentionally ignored even though they can implement language structure, copying support, and reasoning computation beyond factual memory.
The claimed midpoint rift is observed in one 32-layer model without depth-normalized replication across scales or architectures.
No comparison of direct-answer versus CoT runs tests which circuits are uniquely induced by externalized reasoning.
failure_modes: A probe memorizes dataset or token-position cues and is interpreted as relational information movement.
A head's direct-logit projection names the answer even though downstream residual composition cancels or repurposes it.
Mean ablation creates off-distribution states and backup heads, distorting functional attribution.
Attention-path tracing follows a high-weight edge that carries irrelevant value information.
Free-form or erroneous reasoning uses MLP/state mechanisms absent from the templated correct traces.
reusable_insights: Choose synthetic tasks that separate stored world knowledge from in-context relations, but replicate on natural tasks before generalizing.
Treat parallel/backup routes as a first-class circuit property and intervene on complete path sets rather than single heads.
Triangulate patching, probing, vocabulary projection, and behavioral ablation, while labeling which evidence is causal versus correlational.
Compare information sources across generation steps to test whether the model actually consumes its own intermediate text.
Validate apparent layer phase changes across model depths using normalized layer coordinates and preregistered metrics.
open_questions: Do the proposed pathways remain necessary and sufficient under causal scrubbing of values, positions, heads, and MLPs?
How do circuits differ between CoT and direct-answer prompting on matched questions?
Does the layer-16 transition replicate across Llama versions, scales, architectures, tasks, and erroneous traces?
Which internal computations are faithfully externalized in generated CoT and which bypass it?
Can sparse feature-level interventions distinguish genuine relation composition from same-token copying?

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Revealing the Mystery behind Chain of Thought: A Theoretical Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: Feng et al. use circuit-complexity arguments to explain why external steps increase transformer computational power. The target paper instead proposes concrete component-level pathways in a pretrained 7B model, without proving that they implement the theoretical algorithm.

competitive_landscape.title: Backward Chaining Circuits in a Transformer Trained on a Symbolic Reasoning Task
competitive_landscape.difference: Brinkmann et al. obtain stronger correlational and causal evidence for a depth-bounded backward-chaining algorithm in a small transformer trained on one symbolic task. The target paper sacrifices controllability for a pretrained Llama and emphasizes parallel redundancy and generated-context use.

competitive_landscape.title: Iteration Head: A Mechanistic Study of Chain-of-Thought
competitive_landscape.difference: Cabannes et al. train controlled transformers and isolate an iteration head whose emergence and transfer support iterative algorithms. The target study analyzes an existing LLM's diffuse multi-path mechanism rather than a clean specialized circuit.

competitive_landscape.title: Finite State Automata Inside Transformers with Chain-of-Thought: A Mechanistic Study on State Tracking
competitive_landscape.difference: This later work locates state-tracking circuits and late-layer MLP neurons in controlled Transformer+CoT models, directly challenging the target paper's attention-centric scope and extending evaluation to skipped steps, noise, and length generalization.

competitive_landscape.title: How does Chain of Thought Think? Mechanistic Interpretability of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Sparse Autoencoding
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen et al. use sparse features and activation patching on GSM8K to compare CoT and no-CoT, offering feature-level causal evidence and a scale contrast. The target paper provides richer token-source pathways but weaker faithfulness and natural-task evidence.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first in-depth neural-component account of CoT in an LLM, identifying shared induction-like heads, parallel answer routes, generated-context use, and a middle-layer functional rift.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Sections 4-6 combine head patching/ablation, ontology probes, direct-logit projections, and recursive attention tracing in Llama-2 7B.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: At its February 2024 release, applying circuit-style diagnostics to pretrained-LLM CoT and categorizing parallel answer sources was early and useful. Later controlled and sparse-feature work supplies cleaner causal algorithms. The paper should be read as an exploratory multi-method map, not a validated complete mechanism or general proof of CoT faithfulness.

reviewer_notes: Read all 30 cached pages, including task templates, patching score, head statistics, tracing algorithm, attention visualizations, and limitations. Primary arXiv/OpenReview competitors through 2025 were checked on 2026-08-23. The review explicitly separates causal head-ablation evidence from probing, logit-lens, and attention-flow inference.
